questions.question: What is the primary purpose of DNS (Domain Name System)?
options: To encrypt data between browser and server
To translate domain names (like example.com) into IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS translates human-readable domain names (like example.com) into IP addresses (like 192.0.2.1) that computers use to locate servers on the internet.

questions.question: What is the main difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
options: HTTPS encrypts data in transit, while HTTP sends data in plain text
HTTP only works on mobile devices
questions.explanation: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts data in transit using TLS/SSL, while HTTP sends data in plain text, making it vulnerable to interception.

questions.question: Put these steps in the correct order for loading a webpage:
options: DNS lookup → TCP/TLS connection → HTTP request → HTML response
HTTP request → DNS lookup → TCP/TLS connection → HTML response
TCP/TLS connection → DNS lookup → HTTP request → HTML response
HTML response → DNS lookup → HTTP request → TCP/TLS connection
questions.explanation: The correct order is: 1) DNS lookup (translate domain to IP), 2) TCP/TLS connection (establish secure connection), 3) HTTP request (request the page), 4) HTML response (server sends the page).

questions.question: Which of the following are valid HTML5 semantic elements? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, and <footer> are all semantic HTML5 elements that provide meaning to the structure. <div> and <span> are generic containers without semantic meaning.

questions.question:
What is wrong with this HTML form code?

```html
<form action="/submit">
  <input type="text" name="email">
  <button>Submit</button>
</form>
```
options: The form is missing a method attribute
The input is missing a label
Nothing is wrong with this code
questions.explanation: The form is missing a method attribute (should be method="post" or method="get"), and the input is missing a label for accessibility. While the code would work, it's not best practice.

questions.question: Which HTML code correctly creates a link to an external website that opens in a new tab?
questions.explanation: To open a link in a new tab, you use target="_blank" on the anchor tag. The correct syntax is: Link

questions.question: What HTML code would create an image with proper accessibility?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text for screen readers and when images fail to load. It should be descriptive of the image content, not just generic text like 'Photo'.

questions.question: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: ID selectors (#id) have the highest specificity (100 points), followed by class selectors (.class) with 10 points, and element selectors (div) with 1 point.

questions.question: Which CSS properties are part of the box model? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The box model consists of: content (width/height), padding (space inside), border, and margin (space outside). Color and font-size are not part of the box model.

With content-box, width is just the content. Total width = content (200px) + padding left (20px) + padding right (20px) + border left (5px) + border right (5px) = 250px. Margin is not included in the width calculation.

questions.question: If we add `box-sizing: border-box;` to the .box from the previous question, what is the content width now?
questions.explanation: With border-box, the width (200px) includes padding and border. Content width = 200px - padding left (20px) - padding right (20px) - border left (5px) - border right (5px) = 150px.

questions.question: Which CSS code would center a flex container's items both horizontally and vertically?
options: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;
questions.explanation: To center items both horizontally and vertically in flexbox: justify-content: center (horizontal/main axis) and align-items: center (vertical/cross axis).

options: A grid with 3 equal columns and 20px gap
A grid with 3 columns (middle column is twice as wide as the side columns) and 20px gap
A grid with 2 columns and 20px gap
A grid with 1 column and 20px gap
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr creates 3 columns where the middle column takes up twice the space of the side columns. The 'fr' unit represents a fraction of available space. gap: 20px adds 20px spacing between grid items.

questions.question: Which media query would apply styles only to screens wider than 768px?
questions.explanation: min-width: 768px means 'minimum width of 768px', so it applies to screens 768px and wider. max-width applies to screens smaller than or equal to the value.

questions.question: What CSS units are relative units? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Relative units: em (relative to parent font-size), rem (relative to root font-size), % (relative to parent), vw (viewport width), vh (viewport height). px and pt are absolute units.

margin has 3 values but should have 4
questions.explanation: font-size: 16 is missing a unit. It should be font-size: 16px (or em, rem, etc.). The margin shorthand with 3 values is valid (top, left/right, bottom).

questions.question: Which CSS selector would select a link only when it's being hovered?
questions.explanation: The :hover pseudo-class selects an element when the mouse is over it. The correct syntax is a:hover (single colon for pseudo-classes).

questions.question: What are the four main design principles (PARC)?
questions.explanation: The four main design principles are: Proximity (group related items), Alignment (align elements), Repetition (repeat visual elements), and Contrast (create visual hierarchy).

questions.question: Which box model properties help create proximity and alignment?
questions.explanation: Padding and margin control spacing around elements. Margin creates space between elements (proximity), and both can be used to create alignment and control visual relationships.

questions.question: Which of the following are accessibility best practices? (Select all that apply)
options: Use proper heading hierarchy (h1, h2, h3)
questions.explanation: All of these are accessibility best practices: semantic HTML provides structure, alt text helps screen readers, heading hierarchy aids navigation, keyboard navigation is essential for many users, color contrast ensures readability, and labeled inputs help all users understand forms.

questions.question: What should you do if an image is purely decorative and doesn't convey important information?
options: Use the filename as alt text
questions.explanation: For decorative images, use an empty alt attribute (alt=""). This tells screen readers to skip the image, preventing unnecessary announcements while still maintaining valid HTML.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to specify the color red in CSS? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: All of these are valid ways to specify red in CSS: named color (red), hexadecimal (#FF0000), RGB (rgb(255, 0, 0)), RGBA with full opacity (rgba(255, 0, 0, 1)), and HSL (hsl(0, 100%, 50%)).
